title: Nondeterministic automata: from branching paths to exact subsets
prompts: An ε-NFA reads the entire word 01. One possible path consumes both symbols and ends in an accepting state; every other possible path rejects or stops early. What is the result?
The current active set is {q0,q1}. On input 1, q0 has no destination and q1 reaches q2. There are no ε-edges. What is the next active set?
Start at q0; only q2 accepts. There are no ε-edges. q0 on 0→{q0}, on 1→{q0,q1}; q1 on 0→{q2}, on 1→∅; q2 has no symbol destinations. Does the machine accept 101?
The only ε-edges are q0→q1, q1→q0 and q1→q2. What is the ε-closure of {q0}?
A machine contains several ε-edges and an accepting state. What is the ε-closure of the empty active set ∅?
Start at q0; only q2 accepts. The only symbol edge is q0 on 0→q1, and the only ε-edge is q1→q2. After reading the word 0, which closed active set and decision are correct?
An ε-NFA starts at q0, with ε-edges q0→q1 and q1→q2. There are no other ε-edges. What is the start state of its subset-construction DFA?
The NFA accepting set is {q2}. Its reachable subset DFA contains a state whose members are {q0,q2,q3}. How is that DFA state classified?
The subset construction reaches the empty subset ∅. What are its destinations on 0 and 1, even if the original NFA contains ε-cycles?
An ε-NFA has five states. What can be concluded about the number of reachable states in its subset-construction DFA?
Why does the full reachable subset construction recognize the same language as its ε-NFA?

An NFA has no ε-edges. Both q0 and q1 accept; q0 is the start, both symbol moves from q0 go to q1, and both moves from q1 loop to q1. Reachable subset construction yields {q0} and {q1}. Is this necessarily a minimal DFA?
